name: funtrace
baseline: LLVM XRay and uftrace (function-call tracers; gprof -pg style hooks)
workload: Per-call overhead of compiler-inserted function entry/return tracing in a microbenchmark.
claimed_speedup: <10 ns per instrumented call or return; 6x faster than LLVM XRay flight-recorder logging, 15-18x faster than XRay basic logging, 4.5x faster than uftrace
tradeoffs: Needs compiler instrumentation (-finstrument-functions, -pg -mfentry, or XRay); x86-64 Linux only; tracing profiler must be told what to trace; some linker-flag requirements.
caveats: Baselines are XRay and uftrace, not perf/gprof/Valgrind. Benchmark code, CPU and flags not stated on the README page opened. Author says the microbenchmark is 'FWIW' and that uftrace has a different workflow and more features.
found_via: GitHub: WebSearch 'github gprof replacement faster function call tracer C++ README gprof overhead comparison table'

name: Dr. Memory
workload: Memory-error checking of the SPEC CPU2006 suite on Linux, Dr. Memory vs Valgrind.
claimed_speedup: README: 'Dr. Memory is faster than comparable tools, including Valgrind' (chart only, no numbers in text; Valgrind could not run 434.zeusmp and 447.dealII)
tradeoffs: Built on DynamoRIO; supports Windows, Linux, Mac, Android; fewer tool modes than Valgrind (memory checking only).
caveats: Evidence is the CGO 2011 paper 'Practical Memory Checking with Dr. Memory' referenced by the README; the paper and the chart image were not opened (hosts not fetched), so no numbers recorded. Results are from 2011 against an old Valgrind version. License id taken from lgpl-2.1.txt mention on repo page.
found_via: GitHub: WebSearch 'github memory error detector C++ faster than Valgrind memcheck'

name: heaptrack
workload: Heap allocation profiling with stack traces, compared qualitatively with Valgrind massif on larger real-world applications.
claimed_speedup: No numbers in README: 'speed and memory overhead' of heaptrack is significantly lower than massif, multi-threaded apps not serialized, CPU-bound code not slowed
tradeoffs: Linux only; LD_PRELOAD interposition so only allocation-heavy code pays overhead; heap profiling only (no CPU profile); GUI needs Qt/KDE.
caveats: Search snippet of the author's blog claims roughly 10x faster than massif but the blog was not opened, so no number recorded. Tier D kept because the project is widely used.
found_via: GitHub: WebSearch 'memory profiler faster than Valgrind massif heaptrack github C++ overhead'

name: tracing_malloc
workload: Run of an Unreal Engine 4 example server for about 5 s, native vs LD_PRELOAD tracing_malloc vs valgrind.
claimed_speedup: real time 5.375 s native, 6.888 s with tracing_malloc, 53.204 s under valgrind (about 7.7x less wall time than valgrind, derived from page data)
tradeoffs: Linux LD_PRELOAD allocation tracker and leak detector; does not detect invalid accesses like memcheck.
caveats: Single run, no compiler flags, hardware or repeat counts; no LICENSE file found at repo root via raw fetch (license unconfirmed, so marked reference); the tools compare different things (leak tracking vs full memcheck).
found_via: GitHub: WebSearch 'github LD_PRELOAD memory leak detector C++ times faster than Valgrind README benchmark'

name: bytehound
baseline: heaptrack / Valgrind Massif (README says 'other similar tools')
workload: Heap allocation profiling with a custom stack unwinder.
claimed_speedup: 'a lot cheaper than other similar tools, potentially up to orders of magnitude faster in some cases' (no numbers)
tradeoffs: Linux only; Rust implementation usable on C/C++ programs through LD_PRELOAD; can export to heaptrack format.
caveats: Claim names no baseline or numbers; baseline is a best guess. Last commit 2023-07-28.
